$S_N1$ rate depends on the stability of the carbocation, which is most stable when planar ($sp^2$).
IV: $Ph_3C^+$ (trityl) is stabilised by resonance over three phenyl rings, so it is the most stable and reacts fastest.
III: $(CH_3)_3C^+$ is planar and stabilised by $+I$ and hyperconjugation (9 α-H), but has no resonance, so it is slower than IV.
I and II are rigid bridgehead bromides: the bridgehead cation cannot become planar, so it is highly destabilised and both react much more slowly than III.
Bicyclo[2.2.1] (norbornyl, II) is more strained than bicyclo[2.2.2] (I), so its bridgehead cation is the least stable.
Order of rate: $\text{II} < \text{I} < \text{III} < \text{IV}$
Answer: (B)
